focus.label: Age-related posterior corneal degeneration (e.g., posterior crocodile shagreen)
focus.why: Elderly asymptomatic patient with bilateral symmetric posterior stromal rings, no surgery, normal lipid/glucose, coexisting posterior crocodile shagreen, pterygium, and mild lens sclerosis all support an age-related degenerative process.

payload.analysis: Combined with the suspicion of age-related posterior corneal degeneration, in vivo confocal microscopy shows long bandlike structures with thin streaks and no cellular infiltration, consistent with posterior crocodile shagreen; slit-lamp confirms bilateral symmetric ring opacities. Family history and genetic testing remain unavailable, but late onset, asymptomatic course, and normal metabolic screening strongly support a benign degenerative process. All key imaging information is covered.

payload.report: Asymptomatic older man with bilateral symmetric posterior stromal ring opacities, normal metabolic screening, and no surgery. Slit-lamp: smooth non-pigmented rings, normal sensation, peripheral posterior crocodile shagreen. Confocal: long bandlike structures without cellular infiltration. These features are diagnostic of posterior crocodile shagreen, an age-related degeneration. Metabolic, inherited, and inflammatory causes are excluded.
